cls: Antiplatelet agent (P2Y12 ADP receptor inhibitor, thienopyridine)
pharm: Prodrug whose active metabolite irreversibly inhibits platelet P2Y12 ADP receptors, preventing platelet aggregation
quick: ACS: 300 mg load then 75 mg once daily; otherwise 75 mg daily
No clear drug-associated risk; do not withhold for MI/stroke
Limited data; weigh benefits and risks
No dose adjustment; reduced antiplatelet effect in severe impairment
Caution in severe impairment; antiplatelet effect preserved
No specific interaction; avoid excess (bleeding/GI risk)
Signs of bleeding; consider CYP2C19 genotype where relevant
summary: Clopidogrel is an oral P2Y12 platelet inhibitor used to reduce atherothrombotic events in acute coronary syndrome, recent MI or stroke, and established peripheral arterial disease. It is a prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation; a boxed warning notes diminished effect in CYP2C19 poor metabolisers. Its main risk is bleeding.
indications: Acute coronary syndrome (UA/NSTEMI and STEMI) - with aspirin, to reduce MI and stroke
Recent MI, recent stroke, or established peripheral arterial disease - to reduce MI and stroke

dosage.d: 300 mg oral loading dose, then 75 mg once daily
dosage.n: Give with aspirin; omitting load delays effect by several days

dosage.r: Recent MI, recent stroke, or PAD

dosage.n: Reduced active metabolite and antiplatelet effect

admin: Take once daily with or without food
Discontinue 5 days before elective surgery with major bleeding risk
Do not stop prematurely - increases cardiovascular event risk
moa: Clopidogrel is a prodrug; its active metabolite (formed mainly via CYP2C19) irreversibly binds the platelet P2Y12 class of ADP receptors, blocking ADP-mediated activation of the GPIIb/IIIa complex and inhibiting platelet aggregation for the platelet lifespan (7-10 days).

absolute: Active pathological bleeding (e.g. peptic ulcer, intracranial haemorrhage)
Hypersensitivity to clopidogrel or any component
relative: Recent surgery or high bleeding risk
monitor: Platelet count and smear if TTP suspected

preg: Available human data have not identified drug-associated risks of major birth defects or miscarriage. MI and stroke are emergencies - therapy should not be withheld for fetal concerns. Clopidogrel use during labour/delivery increases maternal bleeding; avoid neuraxial blockade and, when possible, discontinue 5-7 days before delivery or neuraxial procedure.
lact: No data on presence in human milk or effects on the breastfed infant; rat studies show clopidogrel/metabolites in milk. Weigh developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential infant risk.
renal: No dose adjustment required. Patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment show reduced inhibition of ADP-induced platelet aggregation (~25%).
hepatic: In severe hepatic impairment, inhibition of platelet aggregation was similar to healthy subjects; use with caution given bleeding diathesis in hepatic disease.

major: Omeprazole / esomeprazole (CYP2C19 inhibitors) - reduce active metabolite and antiplatelet effect; avoid
Strong CYP2C19 inducers (e.g. rifampin) - increase active metabolite and bleeding risk; avoid
moderate: Warfarin - increased bleeding (independent effects on haemostasis)
Opioids - delayed/reduced clopidogrel absorption; consider parenteral antiplatelet in ACS
Repaglinide and other CYP2C8 substrates - increased substrate levels
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (food reduces active metabolite Cmax but not AUC)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; excess increases bleeding/GI risk
interactions.diagnostics: CYP2C19 genotyping and platelet function testing available to identify poor responders

emergency: TTP (thrombocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, neuro signs, renal dysfunction, fever)

monitoring: CBC if bleeding or TTP suspected (platelets, peripheral smear)
CYP2C19 genotype in selected high-risk patients
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed; do not stop without consulting your doctor
Report unusual bleeding, bruising, blood in urine or stool, or severe headache
Tell surgeons/dentists you take clopidogrel; it is usually stopped 5 days before major surgery
Avoid omeprazole/esomeprazole - ask about alternative acid suppressants
Seek urgent care for signs of TTP (fever, weakness, confusion, bruising)
pk: Platelet inhibition detectable ~2 hours after a single oral dose
Steady-state inhibition between days 3 and 7 (40-60% with 75 mg/day)
Active metabolite ~30 minutes; effect lasts platelet lifespan
Irreversible - platelet function recovers over ~5 days after stopping
Store at 20-25 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation - boxed warning for poor metabolisers
Avoid omeprazole/esomeprazole; use pantoprazole if PPI needed
Stop 5 days before major elective surgery
Irreversible effect - manage major bleeding with platelet transfusion
Never stop abruptly after coronary stenting (thrombosis risk)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose; do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose may cause bleeding complications; platelet inhibition is irreversible and lasts the platelet lifespan. Platelet transfusion may help restore clotting. Provide supportive care.
